review_title: Buyer beware - don't make the mistake of buying this product
body_en: I wanted to love this coffee maker so much, I really did. It's definitely a fun design and looks great, and it worked like a charm for a couple of months, but then I started having the same issue that so many others started having when their pot wasn't very old. It started steaming up a storm (literally making the machine soaking wet with steam sweat as it tried to brew) and brewing very, very little coffee... and having a burnt taste to what actually did end up in the pot. On top of that, the carafe is incredibly thin and fragile. My first one cracked by the handle within weeks, and after some teeth pulling I managed to get a replacement from the company... but then, a little over a month later, the brewer itself stopped working. I know I've read about a 1-year warranty, but I honestly don't even think it's worth the hassle trying to get a replacement for a crappy coffee brewer that's just going to crap out on me again after a few months. For example, when I tried to get a replacement carafe... I first contacted Amazon and was told I had to go directly to Nostalgia, so I did. I emailed them first, but after many days did not hear back. I then found a phone number and called. After a looooooong hold time I finally spoke to someone and she was very nice and said she was sending me a new pot (despite their website saying they were out of stock). A day after I spoke to this lady on the phone someone else replied to my email and said they couldn't send me a new carafe. I told her that I spoke to someone who said they would send me a new carafe to which this person basically replied, "so she did." It sounded like the person on the email didn't want to send me a replacement at all despite them actually having them in stock. I'm glad I got someone on the phone, because they did come through... but that's still a bit shady - hence why I don't even feel like dealing with trying to replace the whole crappy unit now that it's crapped out on me. I'm sadly tossing this in the trash and putting money towards a top rated and top notch coffee brewer. No fun nostalgia in my kitchen, design wise, but I'd rather have functionality any day of the week.

review_title: Quality & design issues surfaced during usage
body_en: August 2023 update: On the 3rd week, my 2nd unit started to blink two hard drive connections on and off with only 3 ports switched on. Therefore rating is reduced to 1 star from 2. Initially, my 2nd unit successfully wrote 350 Gb drive to drive across this hub without any buffering errors (buffering errors are what usually goes wrong in such tests). Speed was about 40 - 70 mb per second for nominally-sized files. However was unable to complete a chkdsk on a mounted drive without terminating in a unidentifiable error (again usually what happens with bad hubs). My first unit which was returned had a bad port #3 (counting from the end plugs) and was causing disk errors evident in the Windows event viewer, which actually were errors when chkdsk was used (you cannot always trust the event viewer drive errors as Windows presumes any drive is where you left it from your last Windows session, so if you move it, or it is new to the location on its USD bus, the event viewer will scream bloody murder until it learns the new location, where it will then proclaim the drive is healthy). There appears to be a design deficiency in the hub: on both units I tested, there was too much noise on the final port #10 to plug in a cam. The cam image was very noisy and unusable. Plugging in the cam at the first port works around this design problem. Apparently, there is inadequate noise containment within the hub body, and this can cause slower transfer rates for hard drives and bad images for cams. Given the wide variety of hubs and potential for hub problems, and quality variance of Asian-pacific manufacturers, I am going to keep this one. Be sure to check each port when you receive yours.

review_title: Yeah, this ain't it. Real review right here.
body_en: I wear Maui Jim's, Smiths, and Suncloud (also by Smith). I am used to high quality lenses, but I've always thought that "high quality" lenses were fairly common and easy to make, and I was just aa brand snob. These look exactly like Maui Jim's. I want a new style so... Ordered them. The fit: great. The wright: great. They feel durable. They feel comfortable. The style is great. The lenses: useless and I would honestly say no chance I'd wear these sunglasses. Literally zero chance. Why? 1. Put these on and look at a regular light bulb. Any light bulb at home. You'll see three images of that light bulb, one to the left which is faint, one to the right which is faint, and the bulb itself in the middle. Not joking. It's as if there is a "glare". This is because the lenses are not perfect thickness and magnification, and the lens coating are layered poorly (I am guessing here). Put on a pair of Maui Jim's (or other high end brand) and you'll see just one light bulb. I'm not making this up. Try it. This will affect everything you look at, brighter objects more. 2. Look at these glasses while wearing high end glasses. You'll see the polarization film -- especially around the bridge and arms. Now, look at the high end glasses through these. You wont see the polarization film (it's there, you just can't see it). High end lenses have much better and even polarization. The lenses on these glasses are simply too cheap, the flaws are really noticeable. I wish they were better, really do. I love this rimless style.

review_title: Large pot burns and leaks. Single cup function is great.
body_en: I don't love this coffee maker. The burner is way too hot so if coffee is brewed and in the pot on the burner for longer than 15-20 minutes, it's so hot it will burn me. I have to leave for work and take the lid off my coffee in the car before I can even drink it. Not ideal obviously. And when there's a cup or two left on the burner, it burns in the pot and smells and tastes like nasty gas station coffee, so it's undrinkable and wasted. Also, when you pour water in using the caraffe, it doesn't just drip, it gushes out no matter how slow/fast or what the pouring angle is. I have to pour it into the machine with a towel on the counter. The single cup brewing is the part I like. I haven't tried iced coffee yet, but the instructions basically have you brewing normal coffee into a cup or the caraffe with ice in it. I guess the burner turns off for that part. It would be a really great machine without the overheating and dripping issues and now I've spend $100 buck on it and can't justify getting a new one so here we are.

To this machine's credit, it makes coffee. It’s fast, easy to clean, and it brews from both grounds and pods. It also doesn't take up a lot of counter space. But if you’re hoping for a mess-free morning or actual iced coffee without a chemistry experiment, it might not be for you. If you’re looking for a coffee maker that brews with the intensity of a thousand suns, this one might be your new spazzy companion. The main difference between the regular and iced settings is the volume of coffee dispensed into your mug. I tested each one, and both came out hot enough to steam my glasses. Iced coffee? More like “melted hopes and dreams." If you prefer hot coffee, it works well, but you'll need a couple ice cubes or plenty of time to allow it to cool to drinking temperature. The Bold setting promises flavor, but what it really delivers is splash zone drama. Every brew cycle left my counter looking like a caffeine crime scene. I tried adjusting cup placement, brew size, and even my expectations, none of which stopped the splatter. Overall, for the price, this appliance is a pretty good deal, but if you drink iced coffee, it's no better than a regular coffee maker. I bought these after hearing multiple social media influencers rave about them for months. Finally caved! I subscribed to these strips because it was cheaper. But I was a little lazy lol and didn’t even start trying them out until after I already had FOUR BOXES of them…ok so I was super lazy. I just don’t love the experience of using white strips so I put it off. But after I had 4 boxes I figured I better start using them. I was so certain they’d be great because these influencers rave so much! But there’s so much they don’t tell you. I have only used these, and different types of the Crest white strips in the past, so I only have the Crest to compare them to. First, sensitivity: this is the one area that I would say is purely a pro. These don’t make my teeth cold sensitive at all after use. If your teeth have a really hard time maaaaybe it would be worth all the cons to use these. Whitening: my teeth are getting whiter, 3 boxes in. It’s taking much much longer than the crest white strips took. I always brush my teeth before applying the strips and wear them for 30 min as directed - I use a timer. So I’m using them correctly but the whitening effect is sooooo slow. Not impressed at all. My teeth would get to a nice white after less than 1 box of crest strips. I’ve used 3 boxes of these already and still my teeth are not as white as they should be (and they weren’t horribly stained to begin with). Application: it’s weird I even have to mention this! With the crest strips you just put them on. With these, you dab your teeth super dry, carefully position them, try to put them on, but they flop and slide around, so you have to try to glue them down with pressure but be careful or they’ll slide…it’s annoying. They’re needlessly difficult to get to stick to your teeth. Plus - often during the whitening process the corners will come loose and be annoying sticking out and poking your tongue. The WORST PART: when you take them off. I was expecting a little residue because the strips I’ve used in the past left a little residue. With these basically all the gel stays behind stuck stubbornly on your teeth. Don’t spit in the sink - you will spit out chunks of gel and it feels so disgusting it’s nauseating. The gel thickly coats every tooth and if you have any crooked teeth it will be worse. What I do is use my wet toothbrush (which I don’t like doing since you’re not supposed to get your mouth wet after these strips but nothing else works) to scrub the gel off my teeth. I have to rinse my toothbrush several times because it gets totally gunked up with gel. Then I spit the remaining bits of gel out. It is extremely unpleasant. The first few strips I used, I thought something was wrong with my box but lucky for me I had other boxes, and none of them were old. but just in case, I tried the newest box. No, they’re all like this. All of the strips leave such a thick layer of goo on your teeth I can’t even imagine why the influencers rave over this product. To me, this is something you should use as a last resort lol if you can’t use anything else, ok try this. If you can handle sensitivity or have money for other means of whitening, avoid these!!!! They are so disgusting. I can’t believe people recommend them without even mentioning the mess of goo at the end and the slowwww whitening! These are so not worth the price. I still have some strips to use up, they were too expensive to throw away, but man do I regret buying them. Yuck!

Might be worth using either Razer's provided grips or another brands for long-term use. Overall, it's a very good mouse if it's within your price range, and your hands are moderately large in size. Maybe it's placebo, but I also dropped my first nuke in Call of Duty on keyboard and mouse using it. That might be influencing might personal opinion of it, but I promise it's a great mouse.

review_title: Absolutely Stunning — My Favorite Candle Ever!
body_en: I wasn’t sure what to expect when I ordered this, but the moment I lit it for the first time, I was completely blown away. The Jasmine, Oud & Sandalwood combination is pure sophistication in a candle. It’s warm, exotic, and incredibly inviting — like walking into a high-end spa. The scent throw is phenomenal. One candle fills my entire living room without being overpowering. It hits that perfect balance of strong enough to notice but not so heavy that it gives you a headache. The jasmine adds a fresh floral top note while the oud and sandalwood give it that deep, rich, luxurious warmth underneath. The layers of scent are just chef’s kiss. The burn is incredibly clean and even. No tunneling, no excessive soot, and the wick stays perfectly centered. It burns down slowly too, so you really get your money’s worth out of it. I’ve had cheaper candles burn out in days — this one lasts. The packaging alone feels like a gift. It looks beautiful on my coffee table and gets compliments from every single guest who comes over. People always ask where I got it! If you’re on the fence, just buy it. This is hands down the most luxurious candle I’ve ever owned, and I will be repurchasing without hesitation. Lulu Candles has a customer for life! 🕯️​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

Well worth the money spent. Allows for more usb slots now that newer computers are downsizing the number of slots that they used to come with. No degradation in picture quality through hdmi, doesn't appear to slow down data transfer. Powers on with the computer it attaches to. Plug and play, no driver installation or software. I've only used on Windows computers, but I'm sure if whatever computer has a USB C, it would work. There are slots for charging devices. I bought a lot because there are a lot of employees needing to use it because their hdmi slots are not providing enough power to the output device they are using. They use a SMART board/tv that had a hard time reading the signal from the regular hdmi port. But once plugged into this hub, it had no issues recognizing it and broadcasting a signal.
